taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts A. albiflora and recognizes subsp. texana; Williamson records the old var. texana concept, equivalent to current subsp. texana.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — project Master Plant Pool has a wild Hays-local observation. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index has three A. albiflora specimens. Williamson — county flora documents A. albiflora var. texana, now accepted as A. albiflora subsp. texana.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; infraspecific synonymy reconciled before counting Williamson.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the petals and prickles. White prickly-poppy has large white petals, strongly glaucous blue-green foliage with pale veins, yellow latex, and sharply prickly leaves/capsules.
diagnostic_traits: deeply lobed prickly leaves with pale veins
Texas plants often represented by subsp. texana

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. aurantiaca has yellow-orange flowers. A. sanguinea has rose to red/lavender petals. A. polyanthemos is another white-flowered species but belongs to a more plains/west-central concept and needs capsule/bud characters plus range.
